findings.where: results/within_day_inputs.json outcome_caveat (code/21_within_day_inputs.py, the outcome_caveat f-string, clause 'at the 30%-false operating point ...'), hence outcome_full and every document that quotes it
findings.text: The clause gives wqaW against wqa only ('it warns of 31% with 30% false on the test years, against 25% with 30% false for the AORC rain to midnight alone') and leaves out the control at the same operating point, which the same file stores (operating_points.sets.wqaW_older.l1.rules.far_cap): trigger 1.45, 30.1% warned with 31.3% false (single seeds 27.2% to 31.6%) against wqaW's 30.8% with 29.9% false (single seeds 28.0% to 34.4%, trigger 1.50) and wqa's 24.7% with 29.8% false (23.4% to 28.5%, trigger 1.60). At the one operating point the GO rule cares about, the control with no information about day t is level with the test set, so the reading the clause invites ('the within-day columns add about 6 points at 30% false') does not hold against the control. At trigger 1.0 and at the CSI-chosen level wqaW is above the control (55.6% against 52.7% with fewer false warnings, 50.1% against 56.2%; 59.7% against 52.7%) and its NSE is higher in 12 of 12 basins, so the file's numbers support 'the hours of day t add warnings at the fixed level and nothing at the 30%-false level'. Fix: add the control to the clause ('... against 25% with 30% false for the AORC rain to midnight alone (trigger 1.60) and 30% with 31% false for the older control (trigger 1.45): at this operating point the six columns add nothing over the control') and quote the three numbers together wherever the 30%-false point is cited.

findings.where: results/within_day_inputs.json outcome_caveat, clause 'AORC is an analysis made after the fact: the within-day columns share the hindsight caveat of the AORC rain to midnight (hindsight at most about 3 points)'; what_was_not_done
findings.text: The bound of about 3 points was measured by the E1b review for the DAILY total (the saved wqa networks given Stage IV, a real-time product, for the issue day on 78 days with 171 onsets); nothing of the kind exists for the six within-day columns, and what_was_not_done does not list it. The channel is the same (in the test years AORC's hours are Stage IV's hours times one factor per gauge day, hourly correlation 0.9995: E1b review, observation 1), so the extension is plausible, but as written it is a claim, not a measurement. Fix: 'share the hindsight channel of the AORC rain to midnight (one factor per gauge day); the bound of about 3 points was measured for the daily total, not for these columns', and add to what_was_not_done 'a Stage IV test of the saved wqaW networks with the within-day columns rebuilt from Stage IV hours (the a8 test of the E1b review; data/aorc/stage_iv_hindsight.csv holds 1,800 Stage IV hours of the builder's 50 days to start from)'.

All training years (1980-10 to 2000-09) lie before 2002, where AORC's hours are daily totals spread over the hours by the shape of older radar, satellite or model products (MDR, NOWrad, Stage II, CMORPH, CFSR: the AORC v1.1 methods as read by the E1b review), while the test years' hours have Stage IV's hourly shape; the validation years 2000-2005 straddle the change. The networks therefore learned 'the rain of the last 3, 6 and 12 hours', 'the wettest hour' and 'the wet hours' from hours of another, and in the 1980s poorer, source than the hours they were scored on. The figure footer says 'hours before 2002 are disaggregated daily totals'; outcome_full does not, and the effect on the +4.4 points was not measured. Fix: one clause in outcome_caveat ('the networks learned the within-day columns on hours that are daily totals spread by older products, all training years lying before 2002, and were scored on Stage IV-shaped hours; what this does to the gain was not measured') and an entry in what_was_not_done.

findings.where: results/within_day_inputs.json outcome_caveat, clause 'the control is flat (53% against 51%)' (code/21_within_day_inputs.py outcome_caveat f-string)
findings.text: 'Flat' holds for onsets warned at trigger 1.0 by the seed rule (the pre-registered reading), but the sentence does not say that the control is noisier: 56.2% of its onset warnings are false against 50.4% for wqa (414 against 318 false alarms), its median NSE is 0.736 against 0.767 (higher in 2 of 12 basins, p = 0.064; seed 4 at 0.54): the six older columns cost skill while adding warnings. Fix: 'the control is flat on onsets warned (53% against 51%) and noisier (56% false against 50%; median NSE 0.74 against 0.77)'; the +2.9 points of wqaW over the control at trigger 1.0 come with 6 points fewer false warnings, which the outcome may say.

The seed-by-seed difference lists are built with zip() over the two sets' seed lists; where a five-seed set is compared with a three-seed stored set (within_day_columns: wqaW against wqa; within_day_with_the_forecast: wqaWF_sub against wqaF_sub) they hold three entries (seeds 0-2: [-5.1, 7.9, 9.7] points at lead 1) and seeds 3 and 4 of the new set are silently dropped; nothing in the JSON says so (only the docstring of pair_reading). findings.text: The sentence gives the shares ('from 45% to 42% ... at 2 and 3 days from 39% to 33% and from 37% to 34%'); the paired counts show a loss at 2 and 3 days (15 onsets warned only with the within-day columns against 70 only without at lead 2, sign p = 1e-09; 19 against 56 at lead 3) and at lead 1 (34 against 52, p = 0.07), while by the seed rule it is 'no clear difference' at every lead (the ranges overlap) and the lead-1 NSE is higher (0.723 against 0.693). A reader may want the reading beside the shares: on top of the substituted forecast the within-day columns do not help and by the paired counts cost onsets at 2-3 days.

Both say 'NOT YET REVIEWED', true when they were written; the script sets 'reviewed: results/review_within_day_inputs.json exists' only on its next pass. After the wording fixes run the script with --rescore --seeds 5 --with-forecast (nothing trained; it refuses if a saved file changed) so that the status, the figure header and the fixed clauses are rebuilt together.

The success rule fails with the five seeds and would fail with the first three as well (wqaW seeds 0-2: 50.2%, 56.5%, 58.3% against wqa's 48.6% to 55.3% and the control's seeds 0-2 49.9% to 53.8%): seeds [0, 3] of wqaW sit below the best seed of wqa (55.3%) and of the control (53.8%). The seed count did not decide the verdict.

On the validation years wqaW shows no gain: onsets warned 50.0% against 50.8% for wqa at trigger 1.0 (seed means), best validation NSE of the stopping point 0.411-0.429 against 0.427-0.429 for wqa's three seeds. The test-year gain of +4.4 points is not foreshadowed by the validation years, which fits the rule's reading 'no clear difference' and argues against reading the +4.4 as established.

verdict_text: Every number of results/within_day_inputs.json that I recomputed from results/preds with my own scoring equals the file's (5364 values at 1e-9: the headline of the seven sets at three leads, every single seed, the seed ranges and the seed rule, the per-basin picture, the Wilcoxon and sign tests, the paired onsets, the closure, the validation-chosen CSI and 30%-false triggers with their test scores and verdict words, the little-rain slices, the stored sets' own files); the 14 clauses of outcome_full rebuilt from my numbers are in the text word for word; the 20 saved networks rebuilt from their files reproduce the stored forecasts bit for bit on tables built as the script builds them and to 8e-6 mm/day (same warnings, same NSE) on tables from my own columns; those columns, rebuilt by another route from the hourly cache, equal the project's to 6e-11 mm, every hour of day t ends at or before 24:00 local of day t on every day including the 68 clock-change days, the hour ending exactly 24:00 belongs to day t, and made-up hours and made-up values after a cut day change no earlier forecast (36 + 10 cases); Q95, the scalers and the stopping point come from the training and validation years, the triggers from the validation years, and the script was fixed (hash) before the first training. The experiment's own reading stands: the pre-registered rule is not met (55.6% warned against 51.2%, single trainings 50.2% to 58.3% against 48.6% to 55.3%), and would not be met with three seeds either. One must-fix of wording: at the 30%-false operating point the control with no information about day t (30.1% warned, 31.3% false) is level with wqaW (30.8%, 29.9%), and the sentence gives only wqa (24.7%) there. The should-fix items are wording and record-keeping: the 3-point hindsight bound was measured for the daily total and is extended to the within-day columns without a measurement; the training years' hours (all before 2002) have another hourly shape than the test years'; the control's higher false share and lower NSE, wqaQ's lower NSE, the failed pre-registered expectation about the little-rain onsets, the zip-truncated seed-by-seed lists, the imprecise 'fixed in NEXT_EXPERIMENTS' clause, a stale what_was_not_done entry and a hand-typed 51% in the figure footer.

findings.where: results/within_day_inputs.json choices_made_after_looking_at_test_scores (code/21_within_day_inputs.py CHOICES); every document that quotes E4b
findings.text: The file does not disclose that its three comparison sets (lstm_wqa, lstm_wqaF_sub, lstm_wqaP) gained seeds 3 and 4 on 30 October 2026, after this file's test scores were known (the +4.4 points of 29 October). Every comparison with them, and the success rule 'wqaW above wqa ... in every seed', now runs over five seeds of the base. Its second entry, 'One training pass ... went straight to five seeds per set; no --extend pass exists', is true only of the four new sets. The change moved the headline from +4.4 to +3.9 points (wqa 51.2% to 51.7%, 313 to 316 hits) and the closure of the gap to wqaP from 30% to 26%. It also moved wqa's validation-chosen CSI trigger from 1.00 (51% with 50% false) to 1.05 (48% with 48% false) and its 30%-false point from 1.60 (25%, 30% false) to 1.55 (26%, 32% false). Fix: add a CHOICES entry, for example: 'The stored comparison sets lstm_wqa, lstm_wqaF_sub and lstm_wqaP gained seeds 3 and 4 on 30 October 2026 on a second machine (scripts 16 and 18, see their SEED_NOTE), after this file's three-seed comparison was known (+4.4 points); they are five-seed means since; the success rule's verdict is the same with the three-seed base (the best wqa seed is seed 0, 55.3%).' Change the second entry to 'for the four sets of this script'. Then rescore.

Two texts still describe three-seed stored sets. design.success_rule and e4b_success.rule say 'every single seed of lstm_wqa (stored, three seeds)', but the rule is now evaluated against five (e4b_success.n_seeds.wqa = 5). Every readings.<pair>.how_to_read says 'a five-seed set against a three-seed stored set gives three entries, seeds 3 and 4 of the new set are not in these lists', but seeds_paired is now [0, 1, 2, 3, 4] everywhere and the lists have five entries. Fix: build both texts from the seed lists (for example 'stored, {len(STORED[n]["seeds"])} seeds'; drop the three-entry sentence when every pair has equal seed lists).

findings.where: code/21_within_day_inputs.py, the review guard (same_record, stored_changed, review_covers, review_line)
findings.text: After round_2 is appended, the next --rescore will claim coverage on the wrong grounds. The record's sha256 changes, so same_record turns False and the earlier finding (stored_sets_changed_since_the_review) is no longer carried. stored_changed then compares the stored files only with the previous results file, whose stored_sets_read already holds the five-seed hashes, so it is empty. review_covers becomes True and review_line quotes the ROUND-1 verdict and counts (15 findings, 5364 values). The same happens after ANY edit of the record, including a round that finds the numbers wrong. Fix: compare STORED_NOW with the hashes the review itself recorded (round_2['stored_sets_reviewed'], or round 1's when there is no round_2), and take who, date, verdict and counts from the latest round.

The success rule fails with the five-seed base as it failed with three. wqaW's seeds 0 and 3 (50.2%, 52.7%) sit below the best wqa seed, which is seed 0 (55.3%, an original seed), and below the control's best (53.8%). The added seeds 3-4 of wqa (52.5%, 49.3%) do not decide the verdict.

The slices are the same onsets (220 / 391), and the new sets' shares are unchanged. wqa's share is 80.5% in the little-rain slice (the same as with three seeds) and 35.5% outside it. The reading 'the gain sits in the wetter onsets, the opposite of the expectation' still holds by my numbers.

Read by eye: header 'five seeds per new set, five per stored set', five dots on every bar, footer '52% of wqa' (taken from the JSON since the round-1 fix), status line NOT YET REVIEWED. Bar tops agree with summary_test by eye.

round_2.verdict_text: Every number of results/within_day_inputs.json that depends on the stored sets reproduces exactly from results/preds with my own scoring (5526 values, 0 mismatches). wqaW warns of 340 of 611 onsets (55.6%) against 316 (51.7%) for the five-seed wqa, +3.9 points, with 64 onsets warned only with the within-day columns and 40 only without them. The control is flat (52.7%). At the 30%-false point wqaW gives 30.8% (trigger 1.50) against 25.9% for wqa (1.55) and 30.1% for the control (1.45). The success rule is not met. The little-rain slices are 220 / 391 onsets at 80% to 72% and 36% to 47%. The four new sets' files are byte-identical to 29 October and their own numbers are unchanged (9331 leaves). Every clause of outcome_full, rebuilt from my numbers, is in the text. The fixes are about the record: it does not disclose that the comparison sets gained seeds 3-4 after its test scores were known (must-fix), two texts still describe three-seed stored sets, and the script's review guard would treat any later edit of the record as covering the numbers.
